transcript: One tiny hilltop country survived every single empire. It's called San Marino, and Italy wraps around it completely. Legend says a stonemason named Marinus climbed this mountain around three oh one and just stayed. Rome fell. Popes and dukes rose. You'd think someone would simply walk up the hill. [short pause] A few did. Cesare Borgia held it briefly. A cardinal occupied it in seventeen thirty-nine. Both times, it got its freedom back. Then Napoleon arrives, conquering everything nearby, and offers San Marino more land. [deadpan] It says no thanks. Bigger means noticed. Noticed means conquered. During Italian unification, it had already sheltered Garibaldi, the movement's hero, while Austrian troops hunted him. So the new Italy signed a friendship treaty instead of a takeover. Today it still picks two leaders every six months, like a club that takes its minutes very seriously. One tiny hilltop country survived every single empire, [short pause] mostly by politely asking for nothing.
